content_voiceover: This table is the master reference for porphyrias, memorize the pattern, not every cell. Two big categories: neurovisceral porphyrias, from earlier cytosolic enzyme defects like ALA dehydratase porphyria and acute intermittent porphyria, where ALA and porphobilinogen accumulate; and photosensitive porphyrias, from later defects like congenital erythropoietic porphyria, porphyria cutanea tarda, and erythropoietic protoporphyria, where photoactive porphyrins deposit in skin. The middle enzymes, coproporphyrinogen oxidase and protoporphyrinogen oxidase, cause hereditary coproporphyria and variegate porphyria, with mixed neurovisceral-plus-photosensitive disease. Most porphyrias are autosomal dominant, except ALA dehydratase porphyria and congenital erythropoietic porphyria, which are recessive, and erythropoietic protoporphyria, which is pseudodominant. Tissue source matters, liver porphyrias like AIP and PCT excrete precursors in urine; erythropoietic ones, CEP and EPP, arise in bone marrow, and EPP uniquely excretes protoporphyrin in feces, since it's not water soluble. The two boards-favorite porphyrias are AIP, the classic acute neurovisceral one, and PCT, the most common and classic cutaneous one.
keypoints: Early enzyme defects (ALA, PBG) -> neurovisceral (AIP, ADP)
Late enzyme defects -> photosensitive (CEP, PCT, EPP)
Most AD except ADP & CEP (AR); EPP = pseudodominant
Liver source -> urine excretion; marrow source (EPP) -> feces
keypoint_voiceover: Organize the porphyrias by where the enzyme defect sits in the pathway. Early cytosolic defects, ALA dehydratase porphyria and AIP, cause neurovisceral disease from ALA and PBG accumulation. Late defects, CEP, PCT, and EPP, cause photosensitivity from porphyrin deposition in skin. Middle defects, hereditary coproporphyria and variegate porphyria, cause a mixed picture. Most are autosomal dominant; know AIP as neurovisceral and PCT as the most common, cutaneous porphyria.
